patterns.name: ARO Landing Zone Accelerator Lifecycle
patterns.description: The structured sequential phases required to strategically design, deploy, and operationalize the ARO landing zone utilizing Cloud Adoption Framework principles.

patternViews.name: Phase 0: Platform Foundation
patternViews.description: The prerequisite phase ensuring that generic shared services (networking, security, identity, governance) are successfully implemented via standard Azure Landing Zones prior to ARO architecture.

patternViews.name: Phase 1: Design Areas and Considerations
patternViews.description: Evaluating critical architectural decisions around multitenancy, identity isolation, core network topology, resource group organization, and explicit security models.

patternViews.name: Phase 2: Accelerator Implementation
patternViews.description: Physically deploying the open-source Azure CLI reference implementation, establishing structural policies, and provisioning the target ARO cluster into the landing zone.

patternViews.name: Phase 3: Operations and Baseline
patternViews.description: Establishing Day-2 operations, continually securing executing workloads via Defender, and ensuring long-term architectural health and cluster upgrades.

practices.name: ARO Landing Zone Connectivity and Deployment Practice
practices.description: Dictates the network topology, connectivity constraints, routing schemas, and actual cluster deployment architectures for Azure Red Hat OpenShift.

alphas.name: ARO Network Topology
alphas.description: The architecture of virtual networks, subnets, DNS configurations, and load balancers enabling secure cluster communication.

states.name: Subnets Planned
states.description: Network boundaries, isolation constraints, and IP addressing are properly calculated.

checklist.name: Allocate primary subnet
checklist.description: Plan a minimum /27 route subnet explicitly to deploy the cluster's master nodes.

checklist.name: Allocate secondary subnet
checklist.description: Plan a minimum /27 route subnet explicitly to deploy the cluster's worker nodes.

checklist.name: Prevent NSG association
checklist.description: Ensure the primary and secondary subnets do not have a network security group associated with them (the cluster creates its own).

checklist.name: Verify non-overlapping IP space
checklist.description: Ensure the secondary subnet and the primary subnet do not overlap with on-premises networks or any other network in Azure.

checklist.name: Plan subnet sizing for scaling
checklist.description: Carefully plan IP addresses and the size of the virtual network subnet to support scaling the cluster and adding nodes.

states.name: Connectivity Designed
states.description: Routing rules, egress paths, and ingress topologies are formally established.

checklist.name: Decide load balancer strategy
checklist.description: Choose between exposing ARO services via public or internal load balancers. Setup internal load balancers in the secondary nodes subnet.

checklist.name: Verify restricted egress limitations
checklist.description: Confirm that public load balancers are not used in a restricted egress cluster to avoid asymmetric routing.

checklist.name: Configure DNS resolution
checklist.description: Decide if CoreDNS will resolve cluster-internal domains directly and forward other domains to the default Azure DNS resolver or custom DNS servers in the virtual network.

checklist.name: Design egress traffic flow
checklist.description: Choose unrestricted egress internet access or restricted egress traffic by adding a user-defined route (UDR) with a 0.0.0.0/0 route to Azure Firewall or an NVA.

checklist.name: Validate egress lockdown function
checklist.description: Ensure the ARO egress lockdown function guarantees access to essential components even if outbound traffic is restricted by a firewall.

checklist.name: Manage outbound SNAT ports
checklist.description: If using unrestricted egress access, plan to carefully manage outbound ports to ensure all available outbound ports are not exhausted.

checklist.name: Design pod isolation
checklist.description: Plan NetworkPolicy objects in the project to indicate the allowed incoming connections, utilizing Red Hat OpenShift software-defined networking (SDN).

checklist.name: Evaluate service mesh
checklist.description: Consider implementing a service mesh for capabilities like traffic management, resiliency, policy enforcement, and observability.

checklist.name: Design global load balancing
checklist.description: Consider utilizing Azure Traffic Manager and Azure Front Door to route traffic across multiple clusters in different Azure regions for resiliency.

states.name: Model Selected
states.description: The core deployment mechanism, CLI templating variables, and endpoint exposure models are decided.

checklist.name: Select endpoint deployment model
checklist.description: Choose strictly between the 'Private API server endpoint and private ingress controller' model or the 'Public API server endpoint and public ingress controller' model.

checklist.name: Verify private cluster requirements
checklist.description: If choosing private clusters, verify that the ARO API is exposed exclusively over a private IP address and not a public one.

states.name: Cluster Provisioned
states.description: The ARO cluster is actively running and operationally healthy in the Azure Landing Zone.

checklist.name: Deploy cluster resources
checklist.description: Execute the ARO landing zone accelerator deployment via the open-source Azure CLI reference implementation templates.

checklist.name: Validate core services
checklist.description: Ensure master and worker nodes successfully deploy and report healthy status in the designated primary and secondary subnets.

checklist.name: Validate connectivity profiles
checklist.description: Confirm that all pods in the Azure Red Hat OpenShift cluster can send and receive traffic without foundational limitations, validating the core SDN.

activities.name: Design Network Connectivity
activities.description: Calculates subnets, architects DNS flows, and designs load balancers to ensure the cluster can communicate securely without overlap.

activities.name: Deploy ARO Cluster
activities.description: Executes the deployment of the OpenShift cluster utilizing the Microsoft-recommended reference implementation over the Azure CLI.

practices.name: ARO Landing Zone Governance and Identity Practice
practices.description: Establishes identity, security governance, and resource organization for Azure Red Hat OpenShift landing zones. Focuses on the Value and Solution spaces by defining tenancy, policy enforcement, and multitenancy controls.

alphas.name: ARO Identity Management
alphas.description: The configuration and management of identities, service principals, and access controls for the ARO cluster.

states.name: Design Determined
states.description: Identity and access management approach is decided.

checklist.name: Decide service principal creation method
checklist.description: Determine whether to manually create the service principal or automatically create it during cluster deployment.

checklist.name: Decide authentication mechanism
checklist.description: Choose between Client certificates and Microsoft Entra ID for authenticating cluster access.

checklist.name: Decide multitenancy isolation method
checklist.description: Choose an isolation method: Red Hat OpenShift projects, network policy, or cluster boundaries.

checklist.name: Define RBAC roles and scope
checklist.description: Determine the OpenShift projects, project roles, cluster roles, and compute allocation per application team.

checklist.name: Determine SRE permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) to administer and troubleshoot the entire cluster.

checklist.name: Determine SecOps permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for security operations (SecOps).

checklist.name: Determine Owner permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for the landing zone owner.

checklist.name: Determine App Team permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for application teams to deploy to the cluster, including determining if teams can read other OpenShift projects.

checklist.name: Determine secret storage approach
checklist.description: Decide between Base64 encoded Kubernetes secrets or using a secret store provider such as Azure Key Vault Provider for Secrets Store CSI Driver.

states.name: Access Configured
states.description: Roles, identity bindings, and least-privilege access are logically implemented.

checklist.name: Create cluster service principal
checklist.description: Create a service principal and define custom Azure RBAC roles for the landing zone to simplify permission management.

checklist.name: Configure Microsoft Entra integration
checklist.description: Use Microsoft Entra ID to authenticate users in the ARO cluster.

checklist.name: Define OpenShift projects
checklist.description: Restrict RBAC privileges and isolate workloads by defining explicit OpenShift projects.

checklist.name: Implement OpenShift RBAC
checklist.description: Define required RBAC roles scoped to either a local project scope or a full cluster scope.

checklist.name: Create role bindings
checklist.description: Create role bindings tied directly to Microsoft Entra groups for SRE, SecOps, and developer access.

checklist.name: Minimize administrator rights
checklist.description: Limit user rights and minimize the number of users with administrator rights to protect configuration and secrets access.

checklist.name: Implement Just-In-Time access
checklist.description: Give full access only as needed and just-in-time using Privileged Identity Management in Microsoft Entra ID.

checklist.name: Configure workload identity secrets
checklist.description: For applications requiring sensitive information, use a service principal and the Azure Key Vault Provider for Secret Store CSI Driver to mount secrets stored in Azure Key Vault to pods.

alphas.name: ARO Resource Organization
alphas.description: The structuring of subscriptions, management groups, container registries, and organizational tags to efficiently manage the ARO environment.

states.name: Hierarchy Designed
states.description: Subscription, management group boundaries, and tenancy models are comprehensively defined.

checklist.name: Decide host management model
checklist.description: Determine if container hosts are centrally managed (reducing landing zone instances) or managed by workload teams (requiring more landing zone instances for segmentation).

checklist.name: Extend management boundaries to related resources
checklist.description: Decide if web application firewalls, key vaults, pipeline build agents, and jump boxes follow the same host management boundary.

checklist.name: Choose a tenancy model
checklist.description: Select from workload team-operated single tenant, technology platforms multitenant, or centrally operated single tenant.

checklist.name: Choose a management group hierarchy
checklist.description: Select a flat, segmented, or hierarchical structure based on portfolio scale, billing, governance, and operational alignment.

checklist.name: Decide container registry solution
checklist.description: Choose between the built-in OpenShift registry, Red Hat Quay, Azure Container Registry, or a third-party container registry.

checklist.name: Decide OCI artifact registry topology
checklist.description: Determine the distribution of registries to workloads and clusters (e.g., one per workload, one per cluster, one for all clusters in the landing zone, or one across multiple landing zones).

checklist.name: Decide Azure Policy scope for registries
checklist.description: Set policy scope at the subscription level, resource group level, or management group level to mandate registry usage.

states.name: Structure Enforced
states.description: Policies and logical resource groupings are actively governing the cluster's placement in the landing zone.

checklist.name: Apply generic Azure landing zone policies
checklist.description: Place subscriptions into appropriate management groups (e.g., Corp vs. Online) to inherently assign governance boundaries.

checklist.name: Define naming and tagging standard
checklist.description: Standardize tags for workload names (workloads supported by cluster), cluster resources (alignment elevation), and host operator (responsible team).

checklist.name: Implement OCI registry policy
checklist.description: Implement a policy requiring a specific OCI artifact registry based strictly on the organization's container registry topology.

alphas.name: ARO Security Posture
alphas.description: The holistic set of security controls, network restrictions, scanning functions, and patching workflows protecting the ARO infrastructure.

states.name: Controls Defined
states.description: Security mechanisms, compliance requirements, and internet-exposure bounds are identified.

checklist.name: Decide control plane access
checklist.description: Determine if the cluster control plane is accessible via the internet (default) or strictly private. Plan IP restrictions if public.

checklist.name: Decide egress traffic control
checklist.description: Determine how to control and secure egress traffic from the ARO cluster using Azure Firewall or another network virtual appliance.

checklist.name: Decide secret management mechanism
checklist.description: Decide whether to use Azure Key Vault Provider for Secrets Store CSI Driver or connect the cluster to Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes and use the Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider extension.

checklist.name: Decide registry network access
checklist.description: Determine if the container registry is accessible via the internet or only within a specific virtual network. Ensure disabling internet access does not break CI pipelines or Defender scanning.

checklist.name: Decide registry sharing bounds
checklist.description: Determine whether the private container registry is shared across multiple landing zones or deployed as a dedicated container registry to each landing zone subscription.

checklist.name: Decide image patching workflow
checklist.description: Determine how container base images and application runtimes will be updated over the container lifecycle (e.g., utilizing Azure Container Registry Tasks).

states.name: Mechanisms Active
states.description: Security monitoring, least privilege bindings, and encryption standards are running and enforced.

checklist.name: Limit config file access
checklist.description: Limit access to the ARO cluster configuration file by integrating with Microsoft Entra ID or an identity provider. Assign cluster-admin or cluster-reader appropriately.

checklist.name: Secure pod access
checklist.description: Provide the least number of permissions to pods; avoid using root or privileged escalation.

checklist.name: Connect Arc-enabled Kubernetes
checklist.description: Connect the ARO cluster to Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes to fetch secrets and manage certificates effectively.

checklist.name: Enable etcd encryption
checklist.description: For ARO 4 clusters, explicitly enable etcd encryption to provide an additional layer of data-at-rest security.

checklist.name: Keep OpenShift updated
checklist.description: Keep clusters on the current and previous generally available minor release of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform to avoid security gaps.

checklist.name: Enforce configuration via Azure Policy
checklist.description: Monitor and enforce cluster configurations dynamically by using the Azure Policy Extension.

checklist.name: Enable Microsoft Defender
checklist.description: Use Microsoft Defender for Containers supported via Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes to secure clusters, containers, and applications.

checklist.name: Scan images for vulnerabilities
checklist.description: Scan container images for vulnerabilities with Microsoft Defender or a third-party image scanning solution.

checklist.name: Deploy dedicated private ACR
checklist.description: Deploy a dedicated and private instance of Azure Container Registry to each landing zone subscription.

checklist.name: Connect Registry via Private Link
checklist.description: Use Private Link for Azure Container Registry to securely connect it to Azure Red Hat OpenShift.

checklist.name: Use Bastion Host
checklist.description: Use a bastion host, or jumpbox, to securely access an Azure Red Hat OpenShift Private Cluster.

alphas.name: Team Cognitive Load
alphas.description: The intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load placed on a team, determining their capacity to own and evolve their systems.

states.name: Unmeasured
states.description: Cognitive load is impacting flow but has not been quantified or formally addressed.

checklist.name: Friction points identified
checklist.description: Symptoms of high cognitive load (e.g., missed deadlines, quality drops, burnout) are recognized by leadership.

states.name: Assessed
states.description: The team's cognitive capacity and current load have been evaluated.

checklist.name: Domain complexity evaluated
checklist.description: The complexity of the business domains owned by the team is documented.

checklist.name: Extraneous load identified
checklist.description: Infrastructure, tooling, and communication overheads dragging down the team are mapped.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: Extraneous cognitive load is actively minimized through platform abstractions.

checklist.name: Platform offloading executed
checklist.description: Non-core responsibilities have been successfully transferred to the platform.

checklist.name: Flow metrics improved

alphas.name: Topology Stream-Aligned Team

states.name: Identified

checklist.name: Value stream mapped

states.name: Formed

checklist.name: Cross-functional staffing complete
checklist.description: The team possesses all necessary competencies to build and run their domain.

checklist.name: Dependencies minimized
checklist.description: Blocking dependencies on other functional silos are eliminated.

states.name: Flowing
states.description: The team consistently delivers value safely and independently.

checklist.name: Independent deployment achieved
checklist.description: The team can deploy to production without external hand-offs.

workProducts.name: Cognitive Load Assessment Report
workProducts.description: A structured analysis of a team's cognitive burden, separating domain complexity from infrastructure friction.

levelsOfDetail.name: Initial Survey
levelsOfDetail.description: Subjective feedback gathered from the team regarding pain points.

checklist.name: Developer satisfaction survey completed

levelsOfDetail.name: Quantified Bottlenecks
levelsOfDetail.description: Specific, actionable metrics tracking the extraneous cognitive load.

checklist.name: Tooling sprawl mapped

checklist.name: Support interruption rate calculated

states.name: Conceptualized

checklist.name: Developer needs synthesized
checklist.description: The minimum capabilities required to reduce cognitive load are listed.

states.name: Bounded

checklist.name: Scope limiters defined
checklist.description: Explicit 'out-of-scope' declarations are documented to prevent feature bloat.

checklist.name: Ad hoc interruptions minimized

checklist.name: Joint goal established

patterns.name: Platform Topology Evolution Lifecycle

practices.name: Scrum Delivery Practice
practices.description: An industry best-practice implementation of the Scrum framework, translating the iterative product development methodology into strict, state-gated operational constructs aligned with the platform adoption baseline.

alphas.name: Sprint
alphas.description: A timeboxed iteration of continuous development, acting as the primary container for all other Scrum events.

states.name: Planned
states.description: The Sprint Goal has been established and the Sprint Backlog is formed.

checklist.name: Sprint Goal Definition
checklist.description: A clear, measurable Sprint Goal has been defined and agreed upon by the Scrum Team.

checklist.name: Sprint Backlog Commitment
checklist.description: The Developers have pulled sufficient Product Backlog Items into the Sprint to meet the Sprint Goal.

states.name: Active
states.description: The Sprint is in progress, and daily coordination is occurring.

checklist.name: Daily Execution
checklist.description: Developers are actively working on Sprint Backlog items and coordinating daily.

states.name: Inspected
states.description: The outcome of the Sprint has been demonstrated and feedback collected.

checklist.name: Sprint Review Conducted
checklist.description: The Increment was presented to stakeholders, and the Product Backlog was adapted as needed.

states.name: Adapted
states.description: The team has reflected on their Way of Working and identified improvements.

checklist.name: Retrospective Completed
checklist.description: Process improvements for the next Sprint have been identified and logged.

states.name: Closed
states.description: The timebox has expired and the Sprint is officially concluded.

checklist.name: Timebox Expiry
checklist.description: The pre-determined time duration of the sprint has elapsed.

alphas.name: Product Backlog
alphas.description: An emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product or platform.

states.name: Initialized
states.description: The Product Goal is defined and initial items are listed.

checklist.name: Product Goal Definition
checklist.description: The long-term objective of the product is clearly stated.

states.name: Refined
states.description: Items are sized, detailed, and ordered accurately.

checklist.name: Backlog Refinement Execution
checklist.description: High-priority items are detailed enough to be selected in Sprint Planning.

states.name: Prioritized
states.description: The backlog is strictly ordered to maximize value delivery.

checklist.name: Value Ordering
checklist.description: The Product Owner has sequenced items based on ROI and stakeholder needs.

alphas.name: Increment
alphas.description: A concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal. Each Increment is additive to all prior Increments and thoroughly verified.

states.name: Conceived
states.description: The desired increment is defined by the Sprint Goal and Sprint Backlog.

checklist.name: Increment Scope Bounded
checklist.description: The requirements for the current increment are frozen within the Sprint Backlog.

states.name: Integrated
states.description: Code and configurations have been merged and successfully integrated into the mainline.

checklist.name: Continuous Integration
checklist.description: Automated pipelines confirm successful integration without regressions.

states.name: Verified
states.description: The increment meets the strict Definition of Done.

checklist.name: Definition of Done Attained
checklist.description: All quality, security, and functional gates required by the Definition of Done are passed.

states.name: Done
states.description: The increment is fully usable and potentially releasable.

checklist.name: Potentially Releasable
checklist.description: The Increment is in a state where the Product Owner can choose to release it instantly.

workProducts.name: Definition of Done Artifact
workProducts.description: A formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product.

levelsOfDetail.name: Defined
levelsOfDetail.description: A baseline checklist of quality criteria is established by the organization and team.

checklist.name: Criteria Documented
checklist.description: Security, performance, and functional criteria are written.

levelsOfDetail.name: Enforced
levelsOfDetail.description: The Definition of Done is strictly applied to every Increment.

checklist.name: Automated Quality Gates
checklist.description: Pipelines programmatically enforce the DoD criteria.

workProducts.name: Product Backlog Item (PBI)
workProducts.description: A single, granular element of work representing value, such as a feature, bug fix, or technical improvement.

levelsOfDetail.name: Drafted
levelsOfDetail.description: A basic title and placeholder description exist.

checklist.name: Identifier and Title
checklist.description: The PBI is logged in the tracking system.

levelsOfDetail.name: Ready
levelsOfDetail.description: The item is clear, small enough to fit in a Sprint, and has acceptance criteria.

checklist.name: Acceptance Criteria
checklist.description: Testable conditions are explicitly written.

checklist.name: Estimated
checklist.description: The item is sized by the Developers.

workProducts.name: Sprint Backlog Board
workProducts.description: The visual and operational manifestation of the Sprint Goal, selected PBIs, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment.

levelsOfDetail.name: Committed
levelsOfDetail.description: The board is populated with the Sprint scope and the Sprint Goal is visible.

checklist.name: Scope Frozen
checklist.description: The backlog items are locked for the iteration duration.

levelsOfDetail.name: In Progress
levelsOfDetail.description: Tasks are actively transitioning through workflow states.

checklist.name: State Updates
checklist.description: Task status is updated daily by Developers.

activities.name: Sprint Planning
activities.description: Initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed. The entire Scrum Team collaborates to establish the Sprint Goal, select PBIs, and form an actionable plan.

activities.name: Daily Scrum
activities.description: A 15-minute event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work.

activities.name: Sprint Review
activities.description: The Scrum Team presents the results of their work to key stakeholders, inspecting the Increment and determining future adaptations to the Product Backlog.

activities.name: Sprint Retrospective
activities.description: The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done, creating a plan for process improvements.

activities.name: Product Backlog Refinement
activities.description: The ongoing act of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items into smaller, more precise items, adding details, estimates, and order.

patterns.name: ARO Landing Zone Accelerator Lifecycle
patterns.description: The structured sequential phases required to strategically design, deploy, and operationalize the ARO landing zone utilizing Cloud Adoption Framework principles.

patternViews.name: Phase 0: Platform Foundation
patternViews.description: The prerequisite phase ensuring that generic shared services (networking, security, identity, governance) are successfully implemented via standard Azure Landing Zones prior to ARO architecture.

patternViews.name: Phase 1: Design Areas and Considerations
patternViews.description: Evaluating critical architectural decisions around multitenancy, identity isolation, core network topology, resource group organization, and explicit security models.

patternViews.name: Phase 2: Accelerator Implementation
patternViews.description: Physically deploying the open-source Azure CLI reference implementation, establishing structural policies, and provisioning the target ARO cluster into the landing zone.

patternViews.name: Phase 3: Operations and Baseline
patternViews.description: Establishing Day-2 operations, continually securing executing workloads via Defender, and ensuring long-term architectural health and cluster upgrades.

name: ARO Landing Zone Connectivity and Deployment Practice
description: Dictates the network topology, connectivity constraints, routing schemas, and actual cluster deployment architectures for Azure Red Hat OpenShift.

alphas.name: ARO Network Topology
alphas.description: The architecture of virtual networks, subnets, DNS configurations, and load balancers enabling secure cluster communication.

states.name: Subnets Planned
states.description: Network boundaries, isolation constraints, and IP addressing are properly calculated.

checklist.name: Allocate primary subnet
checklist.description: Plan a minimum /27 route subnet explicitly to deploy the cluster's master nodes.

checklist.name: Allocate secondary subnet
checklist.description: Plan a minimum /27 route subnet explicitly to deploy the cluster's worker nodes.

checklist.name: Prevent NSG association
checklist.description: Ensure the primary and secondary subnets do not have a network security group associated with them (the cluster creates its own).

checklist.name: Verify non-overlapping IP space
checklist.description: Ensure the secondary subnet and the primary subnet do not overlap with on-premises networks or any other network in Azure.

checklist.name: Plan subnet sizing for scaling
checklist.description: Carefully plan IP addresses and the size of the virtual network subnet to support scaling the cluster and adding nodes.

states.name: Connectivity Designed
states.description: Routing rules, egress paths, and ingress topologies are formally established.

checklist.name: Decide load balancer strategy
checklist.description: Choose between exposing ARO services via public or internal load balancers. Setup internal load balancers in the secondary nodes subnet.

checklist.name: Verify restricted egress limitations
checklist.description: Confirm that public load balancers are not used in a restricted egress cluster to avoid asymmetric routing.

checklist.name: Configure DNS resolution
checklist.description: Decide if CoreDNS will resolve cluster-internal domains directly and forward other domains to the default Azure DNS resolver or custom DNS servers in the virtual network.

checklist.name: Design egress traffic flow
checklist.description: Choose unrestricted egress internet access or restricted egress traffic by adding a user-defined route (UDR) with a 0.0.0.0/0 route to Azure Firewall or an NVA.

checklist.name: Validate egress lockdown function
checklist.description: Ensure the ARO egress lockdown function guarantees access to essential components even if outbound traffic is restricted by a firewall.

checklist.name: Manage outbound SNAT ports
checklist.description: If using unrestricted egress access, plan to carefully manage outbound ports to ensure all available outbound ports are not exhausted.

checklist.name: Design pod isolation
checklist.description: Plan NetworkPolicy objects in the project to indicate the allowed incoming connections, utilizing Red Hat OpenShift software-defined networking (SDN).

checklist.name: Evaluate service mesh
checklist.description: Consider implementing a service mesh for capabilities like traffic management, resiliency, policy enforcement, and observability.

checklist.name: Design global load balancing
checklist.description: Consider utilizing Azure Traffic Manager and Azure Front Door to route traffic across multiple clusters in different Azure regions for resiliency.

alphas.name: ARO Cluster Deployment
alphas.description: The operational state, baseline configurations, and architectural instantiation of the OpenShift cluster nodes and API endpoints.

states.name: Model Selected
states.description: The core deployment mechanism, CLI templating variables, and endpoint exposure models are decided.

checklist.name: Select endpoint deployment model
checklist.description: Choose strictly between the 'Private API server endpoint and private ingress controller' model or the 'Public API server endpoint and public ingress controller' model.

checklist.name: Verify private cluster requirements
checklist.description: If choosing private clusters, verify that the ARO API is exposed exclusively over a private IP address and not a public one.

states.name: Cluster Provisioned
states.description: The ARO cluster is actively running and operationally healthy in the Azure Landing Zone.

checklist.name: Deploy cluster resources
checklist.description: Execute the ARO landing zone accelerator deployment via the open-source Azure CLI reference implementation templates.

checklist.name: Validate core services
checklist.description: Ensure master and worker nodes successfully deploy and report healthy status in the designated primary and secondary subnets.

checklist.name: Validate connectivity profiles
checklist.description: Confirm that all pods in the Azure Red Hat OpenShift cluster can send and receive traffic without foundational limitations, validating the core SDN.

activities.name: Design Network Connectivity
activities.description: Calculates subnets, architects DNS flows, and designs load balancers to ensure the cluster can communicate securely without overlap.

activities.name: Deploy ARO Cluster
activities.description: Executes the deployment of the OpenShift cluster utilizing the Microsoft-recommended reference implementation over the Azure CLI.

workProducts.name: Network Topology Diagram
workProducts.description: The explicit visual and logical map of the VNet, its calculated subnets, firewall routing tables, and ingress endpoints.

levelsOfDetail.name: Defined
levelsOfDetail.description: Detailed workflow flowcharts mapping IP allocation to specific platform components.

checklist.name: IP Addressing Schema
checklist.description: Minimum /27 primary and secondary subnets defined and checked against overlaps.

checklist.name: Egress routes mapped
checklist.description: UDRs (0.0.0.0/0) and required outbound firewall rules logically documented.

workProducts.name: Cluster Sizing Guide
workProducts.description: Calculations and capacity planning documentation dictating ARO node scaling thresholds.

levelsOfDetail.name: Logical
levelsOfDetail.description: Logical modeling of node types and counts selected to accommodate application workloads.

checklist.name: Worker node count logic
checklist.description: Calculated based on workload estimates and memory footprint requirements.

name: ARO Landing Zone Governance and Identity Practice
description: Establishes identity, security governance, and resource organization for Azure Red Hat OpenShift landing zones. Focuses on the Value and Solution spaces by defining tenancy, policy enforcement, and multitenancy controls.

alphas.name: ARO Identity Management
alphas.description: The configuration and management of identities, service principals, and access controls for the ARO cluster.

states.name: Design Determined
states.description: Identity and access management approach is decided.

checklist.name: Decide service principal creation method
checklist.description: Determine whether to manually create the service principal or automatically create it during cluster deployment.

checklist.name: Decide authentication mechanism
checklist.description: Choose between Client certificates and Microsoft Entra ID for authenticating cluster access.

checklist.name: Decide multitenancy isolation method
checklist.description: Choose an isolation method: Red Hat OpenShift projects, network policy, or cluster boundaries.

checklist.name: Define RBAC roles and scope
checklist.description: Determine the OpenShift projects, project roles, cluster roles, and compute allocation per application team.

checklist.name: Determine SRE permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) to administer and troubleshoot the entire cluster.

checklist.name: Determine SecOps permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for security operations (SecOps).

checklist.name: Determine Owner permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for the landing zone owner.

checklist.name: Determine App Team permissions
checklist.description: Decide specific permissions required for application teams to deploy to the cluster, including determining if teams can read other OpenShift projects.

checklist.name: Determine secret storage approach
checklist.description: Decide between Base64 encoded Kubernetes secrets or using a secret store provider such as Azure Key Vault Provider for Secrets Store CSI Driver.

states.name: Access Configured
states.description: Roles, identity bindings, and least-privilege access are logically implemented.

checklist.name: Create cluster service principal
checklist.description: Create a service principal and define custom Azure RBAC roles for the landing zone to simplify permission management.

checklist.name: Configure Microsoft Entra integration
checklist.description: Use Microsoft Entra ID to authenticate users in the ARO cluster.

checklist.name: Define OpenShift projects
checklist.description: Restrict RBAC privileges and isolate workloads by defining explicit OpenShift projects.

checklist.name: Implement OpenShift RBAC
checklist.description: Define required RBAC roles scoped to either a local project scope or a full cluster scope.

checklist.name: Create role bindings
checklist.description: Create role bindings tied directly to Microsoft Entra groups for SRE, SecOps, and developer access.

checklist.name: Minimize administrator rights
checklist.description: Limit user rights and minimize the number of users with administrator rights to protect configuration and secrets access.

checklist.name: Implement Just-In-Time access
checklist.description: Give full access only as needed and just-in-time using Privileged Identity Management in Microsoft Entra ID.

checklist.name: Configure workload identity secrets
checklist.description: For applications requiring sensitive information, use a service principal and the Azure Key Vault Provider for Secret Store CSI Driver to mount secrets stored in Azure Key Vault to pods.

alphas.name: ARO Resource Organization
alphas.description: The structuring of subscriptions, management groups, container registries, and organizational tags to efficiently manage the ARO environment.

states.name: Hierarchy Designed
states.description: Subscription, management group boundaries, and tenancy models are comprehensively defined.

checklist.name: Decide host management model
checklist.description: Determine if container hosts are centrally managed (reducing landing zone instances) or managed by workload teams (requiring more landing zone instances for segmentation).

checklist.name: Extend management boundaries to related resources
checklist.description: Decide if web application firewalls, key vaults, pipeline build agents, and jump boxes follow the same host management boundary.

checklist.name: Choose a tenancy model
checklist.description: Select from workload team-operated single tenant, technology platforms multitenant, or centrally operated single tenant.

checklist.name: Choose a management group hierarchy
checklist.description: Select a flat, segmented, or hierarchical structure based on portfolio scale, billing, governance, and operational alignment.

checklist.name: Decide container registry solution
checklist.description: Choose between the built-in OpenShift registry, Red Hat Quay, Azure Container Registry, or a third-party container registry.

checklist.name: Decide OCI artifact registry topology
checklist.description: Determine the distribution of registries to workloads and clusters (e.g., one per workload, one per cluster, one for all clusters in the landing zone, or one across multiple landing zones).

checklist.name: Decide Azure Policy scope for registries
checklist.description: Set policy scope at the subscription level, resource group level, or management group level to mandate registry usage.

states.name: Structure Enforced
states.description: Policies and logical resource groupings are actively governing the cluster's placement in the landing zone.

checklist.name: Apply generic Azure landing zone policies
checklist.description: Place subscriptions into appropriate management groups (e.g., Corp vs. Online) to inherently assign governance boundaries.

checklist.name: Define naming and tagging standard
checklist.description: Standardize tags for workload names (workloads supported by cluster), cluster resources (alignment elevation), and host operator (responsible team).

checklist.name: Implement OCI registry policy
checklist.description: Implement a policy requiring a specific OCI artifact registry based strictly on the organization's container registry topology.

alphas.name: ARO Security Posture
alphas.description: The holistic set of security controls, network restrictions, scanning functions, and patching workflows protecting the ARO infrastructure.

states.name: Controls Defined
states.description: Security mechanisms, compliance requirements, and internet-exposure bounds are identified.

checklist.name: Decide control plane access
checklist.description: Determine if the cluster control plane is accessible via the internet (default) or strictly private. Plan IP restrictions if public.

checklist.name: Decide egress traffic control
checklist.description: Determine how to control and secure egress traffic from the ARO cluster using Azure Firewall or another network virtual appliance.

checklist.name: Decide secret management mechanism
checklist.description: Decide whether to use Azure Key Vault Provider for Secrets Store CSI Driver or connect the cluster to Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes and use the Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider extension.

checklist.name: Decide registry network access
checklist.description: Determine if the container registry is accessible via the internet or only within a specific virtual network. Ensure disabling internet access does not break CI pipelines or Defender scanning.

checklist.name: Decide registry sharing bounds
checklist.description: Determine whether the private container registry is shared across multiple landing zones or deployed as a dedicated container registry to each landing zone subscription.

checklist.name: Decide image patching workflow
checklist.description: Determine how container base images and application runtimes will be updated over the container lifecycle (e.g., utilizing Azure Container Registry Tasks).

states.name: Mechanisms Active
states.description: Security monitoring, least privilege bindings, and encryption standards are running and enforced.

checklist.name: Limit config file access
checklist.description: Limit access to the ARO cluster configuration file by integrating with Microsoft Entra ID or an identity provider. Assign cluster-admin or cluster-reader appropriately.

checklist.name: Secure pod access
checklist.description: Provide the least number of permissions to pods; avoid using root or privileged escalation.

checklist.name: Connect Arc-enabled Kubernetes
checklist.description: Connect the ARO cluster to Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes to fetch secrets and manage certificates effectively.

checklist.name: Enable etcd encryption
checklist.description: For ARO 4 clusters, explicitly enable etcd encryption to provide an additional layer of data-at-rest security.

states.name: Deployment Model Selected
states.description: The deployment topology (RPM, Containerized, or OpenShift Operator) is selected based on business and infrastructure needs.

checklist.name: Target environment dependencies are reviewed and validated.

states.name: Installation Planned

checklist.description: Configuration files are created and populated with valid credentials and network details based on the chosen deployment model.

states.name: Deployed

checklist.description: The container image is successfully built locally or via CI/CD pipelines without dependency conflicts.

checklist.name: Content navigator validates the environment.
checklist.description: ansible-navigator successfully executes and validates test playbooks against the newly built execution environment.

checklist.name: Execution environments are pushed to the registry.

practices.name: Azure Well-Architected Framework Practice
practices.description: Applies the five pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework (Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, and Performance Efficiency) to design, build, and continually optimize cloud workloads.

alphas.name: Workload Reliability
alphas.description: Ensures the workload meets uptime and recovery targets by building redundancy and resiliency at scale.

states.name: Resiliency Requirements Defined
states.description: Uptime, availability, and recovery requirements are identified and agreed upon with stakeholders.

checklist.name: Define Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO).
checklist.description: Explicitly document the acceptable downtime and data loss metrics.

checklist.name: Identify Critical Flows
checklist.description: Map user journeys and system processes that require the highest availability.

states.name: Redundancy Designed
states.description: Architecture incorporates redundancy across zones, regions, and components.

checklist.name: Eliminate Single Points of Failure
checklist.description: Audit the design to ensure no single component failure can cause system-wide outage.

checklist.name: Incorporate Cloud Design Patterns
checklist.description: Apply reliability patterns such as Bulkhead, Circuit Breaker, and Geode.

states.name: Fault Tolerance Implemented
states.description: The system can gracefully handle failures and self-heal.

checklist.name: Automate Scaling and Self-Healing
checklist.description: Implement automated recovery mechanisms and auto-scaling rules.

alphas.name: Workload Security
alphas.description: Protects the workload from attacks by maintaining confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

states.name: Threats Identified
states.description: Potential attack vectors and security risks are modeled.

checklist.name: Conduct Threat Modeling
checklist.description: Analyze the architecture to identify spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege (STRIDE).

states.name: Identity and Access Configured
states.description: Zero Trust principles are applied, establishing identity as the primary perimeter.

checklist.name: Implement Least Privilege
checklist.description: Configure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) ensuring users and services have only necessary permissions.

states.name: Security Posture Audited
states.description: Security mechanisms are continually verified against baseline policies.

checklist.name: Enable Continuous Security Monitoring
checklist.description: Deploy tools like Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Azure Sentinel.

alphas.name: Workload Cost Optimization

checklist.name: Exclude Major Refactoring
checklist.description: Ensure intensive net-new application development and major legacy refactoring are strictly assigned to the customer's teams, excluding them from the consulting scope.

checklist.name: Exclude Custom CI/CD Elements
checklist.description: Ensure highly customized CI/CD steps beyond a minimally viable workflow are explicitly placed out of scope.

checklist.name: Remove Unintended Expectations Language
checklist.description: Scrub legal scopes of words like 'optimum solution', 'state of the art', 'ensure', and 'success metrics' to avoid unquantifiable subjective perfection clauses.

checklist.name: Remove Guarantee Terminology
checklist.description: Replace phrases like 'guarantee', 'will result in', 'resolve', or 'improve' with cooperative phrasing.

checklist.name: Remove IP and Delivery Traps
checklist.description: Remove terms such as 'deliverable', 'create code', 'jointly develop', and 'intellectual property' to prevent code ownership disputes.

checklist.name: Remove Partnership Implications

checklist.name: Remove IP and Delivery Traps
checklist.description: Remove terms such as 'deliverable', 'create code', 'jointly develop', and 'intellectual property' to prevent code ownership disputes.

name: Site Reliability Engineering Practice
description: A comprehensive operational practice based on 'Site Reliability Engineering' (Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy) adapting industry best practices for platform and asset reliability. Focuses on quantifiable reliability (SLIs/SLOs), error budget enforcement, toil elimination, capacity forecasting, and blameless incident management.

checklist.name: Measurement methodology validated.
checklist.description: The logic to capture SLI data is proven to accurately reflect objective reality.

checklist.name: Stakeholder sign-off achieved.
checklist.description: Product and Engineering agree that the SLO represents the right balance of reliability.

states.name: Monitored
states.description: SLIs are actively tracked and SLO violations trigger alerts.

checklist.description: Real-time visibility into SLI performance vs SLO targets is available.

checklist.name: Burn rate alerting enabled.
checklist.description: Alerts trigger based on the rate of error budget consumption, not just static thresholds.

checklist.description: Feature releases are halted and focus shifts to reliability when the error budget is depleted.

checklist.description: Engineering capacity is explicitly reallocated to fix systemic issues causing budget burn.

states.name: Evolving
states.description: SLOs are periodically reviewed and tightened or loosened based on business needs.

checklist.description: Next-tier reliability targets are simulated to understand architectural requirements.

checklist.name: Historical tuning conducted.
checklist.description: SLOs are adjusted down if users don't notice failures, or up if complaints occur before targets are breached.

description: An industry best-practice implementation of the Scrum framework, translating the iterative product development methodology into strict, state-gated operational constructs aligned with the platform adoption baseline.

alphas.name: Sprint
alphas.description: A timeboxed iteration of continuous development, acting as the primary container for all other Scrum events.

states.name: Planned
states.description: The Sprint Goal has been established and the Sprint Backlog is formed.

checklist.name: Sprint Goal Definition
checklist.description: A clear, measurable Sprint Goal has been defined and agreed upon by the Scrum Team.

checklist.name: Sprint Backlog Commitment
checklist.description: The Developers have pulled sufficient Product Backlog Items into the Sprint to meet the Sprint Goal.

states.name: Active
states.description: The Sprint is in progress, and daily coordination is occurring.

checklist.name: Daily Execution
checklist.description: Developers are actively working on Sprint Backlog items and coordinating daily.

states.name: Inspected
states.description: The outcome of the Sprint has been demonstrated and feedback collected.

checklist.name: Sprint Review Conducted
checklist.description: The Increment was presented to stakeholders, and the Product Backlog was adapted as needed.

states.name: Adapted
states.description: The team has reflected on their Way of Working and identified improvements.

checklist.name: Retrospective Completed
checklist.description: Process improvements for the next Sprint have been identified and logged.

states.name: Closed
states.description: The timebox has expired and the Sprint is officially concluded.

checklist.name: Timebox Expiry
checklist.description: The pre-determined time duration of the sprint has elapsed.

alphas.name: Product Backlog
alphas.description: An emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product or platform.

states.name: Initialized
states.description: The Product Goal is defined and initial items are listed.

checklist.name: Product Goal Definition
checklist.description: The long-term objective of the product is clearly stated.

states.name: Refined
states.description: Items are sized, detailed, and ordered accurately.

checklist.name: Backlog Refinement Execution
checklist.description: High-priority items are detailed enough to be selected in Sprint Planning.

states.name: Prioritized
states.description: The backlog is strictly ordered to maximize value delivery.

checklist.name: Value Ordering
checklist.description: The Product Owner has sequenced items based on ROI and stakeholder needs.

alphas.name: Increment
alphas.description: A concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal. Each Increment is additive to all prior Increments and thoroughly verified.

states.name: Conceived
states.description: The desired increment is defined by the Sprint Goal and Sprint Backlog.

checklist.name: Increment Scope Bounded
checklist.description: The requirements for the current increment are frozen within the Sprint Backlog.

states.name: Integrated
states.description: Code and configurations have been merged and successfully integrated into the mainline.

checklist.name: Continuous Integration
checklist.description: Automated pipelines confirm successful integration without regressions.

states.name: Verified
states.description: The increment meets the strict Definition of Done.

checklist.name: Definition of Done Attained
checklist.description: All quality, security, and functional gates required by the Definition of Done are passed.

states.name: Done
states.description: The increment is fully usable and potentially releasable.

checklist.name: Potentially Releasable
checklist.description: The Increment is in a state where the Product Owner can choose to release it instantly.

workProducts.name: Definition of Done Artifact
workProducts.description: A formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product.

levelsOfDetail.name: Defined
levelsOfDetail.description: A baseline checklist of quality criteria is established by the organization and team.

checklist.name: Criteria Documented
checklist.description: Security, performance, and functional criteria are written.

levelsOfDetail.name: Enforced
levelsOfDetail.description: The Definition of Done is strictly applied to every Increment.

checklist.name: Automated Quality Gates
checklist.description: Pipelines programmatically enforce the DoD criteria.

workProducts.name: Product Backlog Item (PBI)
workProducts.description: A single, granular element of work representing value, such as a feature, bug fix, or technical improvement.

levelsOfDetail.name: Drafted
levelsOfDetail.description: A basic title and placeholder description exist.

checklist.name: Identifier and Title
checklist.description: The PBI is logged in the tracking system.

levelsOfDetail.name: Ready
levelsOfDetail.description: The item is clear, small enough to fit in a Sprint, and has acceptance criteria.

checklist.name: Acceptance Criteria
checklist.description: Testable conditions are explicitly written.

checklist.name: Estimated
checklist.description: The item is sized by the Developers.

workProducts.name: Sprint Backlog Board
workProducts.description: The visual and operational manifestation of the Sprint Goal, selected PBIs, and the actionable plan for delivering the Increment.

levelsOfDetail.name: Committed
levelsOfDetail.description: The board is populated with the Sprint scope and the Sprint Goal is visible.

checklist.name: Scope Frozen
checklist.description: The backlog items are locked for the iteration duration.

levelsOfDetail.name: In Progress
levelsOfDetail.description: Tasks are actively transitioning through workflow states.

checklist.name: State Updates
checklist.description: Task status is updated daily by Developers.

activities.name: Sprint Planning
activities.description: Initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed. The entire Scrum Team collaborates to establish the Sprint Goal, select PBIs, and form an actionable plan.

activities.name: Daily Scrum
activities.description: A 15-minute event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work.

activities.name: Sprint Review
activities.description: The Scrum Team presents the results of their work to key stakeholders, inspecting the Increment and determining future adaptations to the Product Backlog.

activities.name: Sprint Retrospective
activities.description: The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done, creating a plan for process improvements.

activities.name: Product Backlog Refinement
activities.description: The ongoing act of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items into smaller, more precise items, adding details, estimates, and order.

checklist.name: Network Topology Approved

levelsOfDetail.name: Enforced

checklist.description: Automated scripts (e.g., rosa verify quota) pass successfully.

description: Governs the specialized workflows, security constraints, and artifact mirroring required to deploy OpenShift in air-gapped or strictly isolated network environments.

alphas.description: The architectural mitigations addressing the lack of direct internet egress to Red Hat Quay and OperatorHub.

states.name: Isolation Identified
states.description: The strict network boundaries and need for a disconnected install are officially confirmed.

checklist.name: Determine Egress Policy
checklist.description: Validate that the target cluster network cannot reach the internet directly.

checklist.name: Select Mirror Registry Solution
checklist.description: Choose between Red Hat Quay, Nexus, Harbor, or the mirror-registry for Red Hat OpenShift tool.

states.name: Registry Provisioned
states.description: A local mirror registry is actively running and reachable by the isolated network.

checklist.name: Host Provisioned
checklist.description: The virtual machine or appliance hosting the mirror registry is active.

checklist.name: Authentication Established
checklist.description: htpasswd or other authentication mechanisms are enforced on the mirror.

checklist.name: Trust Bundle Distributed
checklist.description: The mirror registry's Certificate Authority (CA) bundle is prepared for cluster injection.

states.name: Payloads Mirrored
states.description: All necessary OpenShift release payloads, cluster operators, and catalog indices are downloaded to the local mirror.

checklist.name: Mirror Release Image
checklist.description: The core OpenShift Container Platform release images are successfully pushed to the local registry.

checklist.name: Mirror Operator Catalogs
checklist.description: The OLM (Operator Lifecycle Manager) catalog index and associated images are mirrored.

states.name: Traffic Redirected
states.description: The cluster is successfully intercepting internet-bound image pulls and redirecting them to the local mirror.

checklist.name: Apply ImageDigestMirrorSet
checklist.description: The ImageDigestMirrorSet (IDMS) or ImageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP) manifests are applied to the cluster.

checklist.name: Update CatalogSources
checklist.description: The cluster OperatorHub is configured to point exclusively to the local mirrored grpc endpoints.

workProducts.name: Mirroring Configuration
workProducts.description: The manifests and command scripts governing the offline synchronization of container images.

levelsOfDetail.name: Identified
levelsOfDetail.description: The target versions, operators, and architectures are listed.

checklist.name: Define OCP Version
checklist.description: The exact target z-stream version (e.g., 4.21.z) is recorded.

checklist.name: Curate Operator List
checklist.description: An exhaustive list of required Operators (e.g., LVM, Serverless, Service Mesh) is established to avoid massive sync times.

levelsOfDetail.name: Mirrored
levelsOfDetail.description: The oc-mirror plugin or legacy mirroring commands have produced the requisite manifests.

checklist.name: Execute oc-mirror
checklist.description: The oc-mirror command completes without fatal errors.

checklist.name: Capture IDMS output
checklist.description: The resulting IDMS yaml files are stored in version control for cluster application.

activities.name: Provision Local Mirror Registry
activities.description: Set up a standalone, highly available container registry inside the secured network boundary.

activities.name: Sync Platform Payloads and Catalogs
activities.description: Utilize the oc-mirror CLI plugin to securely transfer Red Hat content across the air-gap via portable media or bastion hosts.

name: OpenShift Self-Managed Initial Deployment Practice
description: Establishes the foundational requirements, architecture, and procedural workflows for deploying self-managed Red Hat OpenShift 4.21 clusters, encompassing both Installer Provisioned Infrastructure (IPI) and User Provisioned Infrastructure (UPI) methodologies.

alphas.name: Self-Managed Cluster Architecture
alphas.description: The architectural topology and infrastructural parameters defining the self-managed OpenShift installation.

states.name: Topology Selected
states.description: The cluster footprint, high-availability requirements, and underlying infrastructure target (IPI vs UPI) are definitively chosen.

checklist.name: Determine Installation Method
checklist.description: Evaluate and explicitly select between Installer Provisioned Infrastructure (IPI) or User Provisioned Infrastructure (UPI) based on organizational access and automation needs.

checklist.name: Select Underlying Infrastructure
checklist.description: Identify the target environment (e.g., AWS, Azure, Bare Metal, vSphere, Nutanix) for the self-managed deployment.

checklist.name: Define High-Availability Topology
checklist.description: Choose between a standard three-node control plane architecture, a compact three-node cluster, or a single-node OpenShift (SNO) configuration.

states.name: Prerequisites Satisfied
states.description: All infrastructure, networking, and DNS requirements necessary for the OpenShift installation have been met.

checklist.name: Configure Network Routing
checklist.description: Establish proper routing, machine CIDR, and network type (OVN-Kubernetes) configurations.

checklist.name: Establish DNS Records
checklist.description: Create required API and Ingress DNS records pointing to the respective load balancers or node IPs.

checklist.name: Obtain Red Hat Pull Secret
checklist.description: Download the cluster pull secret from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console to authorize container image retrieval.

states.name: Cluster Bootstrapped
states.description: The installation program has successfully executed, creating the control plane nodes and establishing etcd quorum.

checklist.name: Deploy Bootstrap Node
checklist.description: The temporary bootstrap node is provisioned and serves Ignition configurations to the control plane nodes.

checklist.name: Establish etcd Quorum
checklist.description: The control plane nodes successfully join the cluster and form a stable etcd consensus.

checklist.name: Decommission Bootstrap Node
checklist.description: The bootstrap node is successfully removed from the infrastructure once the control plane is self-hosting.

competencies.name: Platform Security And Compliance Enforcement
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, and automate security policies, access controls, and compliance checks within the platform.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands basic security principles and compliance requirements.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can configure basic security settings and access controls based on documented procedures.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can independently design and implement comprehensive security architectures and automate compliance auditing.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can adapt security strategies to address novel threats and complex, multi-cloud environments.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops new paradigms for platform security and proactive threat hunting.

competencies.name: Platform Strategic Alignment
competencies.description: The ability to align platform capabilities and roadmap with broader business goals, economic models, and enterprise architecture.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the high-level business drivers for the platform.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can articulate how specific platform features support identified business opportunities.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can develop and manage platform roadmaps that demonstrably drive business value and ROI.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can pivot platform strategy in response to shifting market conditions or major organizational changes.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Pioneers new platform business models or economic strategies that redefine enterprise value.

competencies.name: Site Reliability
competencies.description: The ability to apply software engineering principles to operations, ensuring platform reliability, scalability, and performance (SRE).

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the concepts of SLIs, SLOs, and basic incident response.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can participate in incident response and implement basic monitoring alerts.

levels.name: Masters

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can architect highly resilient, self-healing systems and establish enterprise-wide SRE practices.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops novel approaches to chaos engineering or predictive reliability modeling.
